summary: Hisao Inagaki (1929–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his BA at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, MA at Ryukoku University, and PhD at SOAS. He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki (1918–1996) studied at Doshisha University (~1938–1941). He held professorships at Kobe University (~1964–1969), Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1969–1982, emeritus), and Komazawa University (~1982–1989).

Hisao Takahashi (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano, later serving on the faculty as assistant (~1977–1982), lecturer (~1990–1998), and professor (~1998–2015).

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and as an associate professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato (1913–2008) was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He was a professor at Kyoto University (1968), Komazawa University (~1977–1984), and Toyo University (~1984–1989), later holding a post at Bukkyo University (~1989–1994).

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, Akira Saito, and others, and held a lecturer position at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Hisatake Kato (1937–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Yamagata University (~1970–1987), Tohoku University (~1987–1992), Tottori University of Environmental Studies, and University of Human Arts and Sciences.

Hitoshi Inui is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held posts at the Research Institute of Esoteric Buddhist Culture (attested 1992) and Koyasan University (attested 1986; professor attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held positions at Otani University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, later serving as professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017).

Hitoshi Miyake (b. 1933) is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at Keio University and the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at Keio University (~1980–1999) and Kokugakuin University (~1999–2004).

Hitoshi Obara (b. 1944) works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hokkaido University and served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1989–2015).

Hla Pe (1913–2007) was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon, University College London, and SOAS University of London. He spent his career at SOAS, teaching Burmese from 1948 and serving as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Washington (completed 1994) under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Hojun Nagasaki (b. 1934) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He was a professor emeritus at Otani University (~1999) and served as president of the Jaina Studies Society in 1998.
Hokai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, where he also served as a professor (attested 1930).
Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She was a doctoral candidate at Harvard University (~2000–2009) and took up a post at the University of Colorado around 2009.

Holmes Welch (1924–1981) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1942–1957) under Francis Woodman Cleaves, later serving as a lecturer at Harvard (~1963–1974) and Yale University.

Hong Luo works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at Peking University and held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center and Sichuan University as a professor.
Hongyue Guo is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Indiana University (attested 2007) supervised by Stephen R. Bokenkamp, having also studied under Xubang Qi.
